html:
A dance and music company founded in Paris in 1952 by the Guinean poet Fodeba Keita, which became the national ballet of Guinea after independence in 1958.

It put on stage the dances, drums and songs of West African villages, with djembe drummers and dancers, and toured Europe, the Americas and Asia. It was one of the first ways audiences abroad saw African performing arts as art rather than folklore. Sekou Toure used it, like the band Bembeya Jazz, to give the new nation a culture of its own. Keita became a minister and was killed at Camp Boiro in 1969.
sum: A dance and music company founded in Paris in 1952 by the Guinean poet Fodeba Keita, which became the national ballet of Guinea after independence in 1958.
